title: Q-WORKERS-200: GATE: start Ultrastable on Ultrastable (6 owner steps)
body:
**Owner:** operations (identity-bound steps are one link in foundation/data/needs-you.json, CONNECT-LINK-1)
**Trigger:** issueloop and queue --run, daily
**Done check:** grep:foundation/data/needs-you.json::dash\.cloudflare\.com
**Status:** open

Moved from ultrastable/workers#200 (workers repo archived; code now under workers/ here, issues disabled on this repo).

The organization starts itself as soon as one door below is done. Until then it stays in dry run and nothing is spent.
A scheduled workflow (`self-start`) re-checks every few hours; nobody has to run anything. No door requires you to write code.

### Let the system create and run the Worker, database and schedule on the new Cloudflare account

Do **any one** of these. They are ordered from least effort to most; the system uses whichever works first.

1. **browser-assisted**, owner effort: sign-in. The owner signs in to Cloudflare once in the browser pane the assistant opens (Continue with Google or GitHub). The assistant then performs every click: Workers and Pages, Create, Import a repository, ultrastable/workers, build and deploy settings, and the database. Consent screens (GitHub app install) are the owner's click.
2. **launcher-temporary-account**, owner effort: clicks. Open the web launcher (apps/launcher), tick the two Cloudflare agreements, and the launcher creates a temporary account, deploys, and gives a claim link to keep it. No token, no terminal.
3. **git-import-by-hand**, owner effort: clicks. In the Cloudflare dashboard: Workers and Pages, Create, Import a repository, choose ultrastable/workers, set the root directory and deploy command shown in docs/SELF-HOSTING.md. Cloudflare creates its own deploy token. Then put the Worker address (https://...workers.dev) in self/worker-url.txt or the SELF_WORKER_URL variable; self-start checks /health and records the start with no token.
4. **api-token**, owner effort: terminal. Create a custom API token (Workers Scripts: Edit, D1: Edit, Account Settings: Read, this account only) and set it as the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN repository secret. Last resort.

### Let the system call a language model with a hard spend limit

Do **any one** of these. They are ordered from least effort to most; the system uses whichever works first.

1. **cloudflare-workers-ai**, owner effort: none. Use the small open models included with the Cloudflare account through the Workers AI binding: no key, no payment, free-plan limits. The router starts on this rung.
2. **provider-key-in-console**, owner effort: typing. Paste a provider key into a console field once; the Worker stores it as a secret and shows only that it exists.
3. **provider-key-secret**, owner effort: terminal. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as a repository secret.

### Let the runner open draft pull requests that trigger CI

Do **any one** of these. They are ordered from least effort to most; the system uses whichever works first.

1. **github-app-install**, owner effort: clicks. Install the Ultrastable GitHub App on the ultrastable organization with one click; it issues short-lived tokens by itself.
2. **fine-grained-token-in-console**, owner effort: typing. Create a fine-grained token limited to the ultrastable repositories and paste it into the console once.
3. **token-secret**, owner effort: terminal. Set SELF_VCS_TOKEN as a repository secret.

### Let the owner open the console

Do **any one** of these. They are ordered from least effort to most; the system uses whichever works first.

1. **generated-first-run**, owner effort: none. The Worker generates a key on first run and shows it once on a first-run page, or sends the owner a sign-in link by email.
2. **access-sso**, owner effort: sign-in. Put Cloudflare Access in front of the console so the owner signs in with their existing Google or GitHub account.
3. **token-secret**, owner effort: terminal. Set SELF_CONSOLE_TOKEN as a repository secret.

## What the system already tried

| Door | Worked | Why |
|---|---|---|
| existing-deployment | no | no https address in SELF_WORKER_URL or self/worker-url.txt |
| workers-builds | no | no successful Workers Builds check run with a workers.dev address on main |
| bootstrap-connect | no | wrangler is not installed here |
| bootstrap-temporary | no | temporary accounts are created by apps/launcher (it deploys with the alarm tick); this script cannot sign a person in |
| bootstrap-scoped-token | no | not set: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN |
| bootstrap | no | dry run: missing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; exit 0 |

## Everything the bootstrapper recorded

| Step | Why only you | If you do nothing | Closes when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Set the GITHUB_TOKEN secret (connector 'github', needed for repo) | a credential only the owner can mint | repo stay in dry-run | `env:GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| Set the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN secret (connector 'cloudflare', needed for runtime, dns) | a credential only the owner can mint | runtime, dns stay in dry-run | `env:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` |
| Set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret (connector 'model_api', needed for agents) | a credential only the owner can mint | agents stay in dry-run | `env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| Approve spending up to 30 USD/month on model and runtime usage | spending money is identity-bound | free tiers only; the fleet logs cost estimates | `manual` |
| Mint the org admin token with the listed scopes | minting the owner's credential is identity-bound | profile content staged in the repo only | `org-manage probe passes` |
| Connect a Cloudflare account (see rungs below) | signing in to Cloudflare is the person's own act; connect: unavailable (wrangler is not installed here); temporary: skipped (temporary accounts are created by apps/launcher (it deploys with the alarm tick); this script cannot sign a person in); scoped-token: unavailable (not set: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) | dry run; every other stage continues | `org/ladder.json route is not null` |
